result.markdown: --- title: "Session 3 — Global Spatial Autocorrelation" subtitle: "Moran's I · permutation test · Moran scatterplot · Geary's C · General G · join counts · Lab 3" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Sessions 1–2: spatial data, maps, neighbours and weights - Today: **is the pattern clustered?** One test for the whole map - By the end you can: - compute and interpret **Moran's I**, with analytic and **permutation** p-values - read the **Moran scatterplot** - choose between **Moran's I, Geary's C, General G and join counts** - **report** a global result in one sentence ::: # Topic 1 — Moran's I {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Are similar values neighbours? ::: {.eq} I = ( n / Σ w~ij~ ) × Σ~i~Σ~j~ w~ij~ (x~i~ − x̄)(x~j~ − x̄) / Σ~i~ (x~i~ − x̄)² ::: ::: {.incremental} - Multiply each area's deviation from the mean by its **neighbours'** average deviation (the **lag**), then scale by the variance - High areas with high neighbours, low with low → products positive → **I > 0** - Expectation with no pattern: **E[I] = −1/(n−1)**, about 0 ::: | I | Meaning | |---|---| | ≈ 0 | no spatial pattern | | clearly > 0 | **clustering**: similar values are neighbours | | clearly < 0 | dispersion: neighbours differ (a checkerboard; rare) | ## Four areas by hand ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} v <- c(1, 2, 9, 10) nb4 <- list(2L, c(1L, 3L), c(2L, 4L), 3L); class(nb4) <- "nb"; attr(nb4, "region.id") <- as.character(1:4) lw4 <- nb2listw(nb4, style = "W"); z <- v - mean(v) c(by_hand = (4 / sum(unlist(lw4$weights))) * sum(z * lag.listw(lw4, z)) / sum(z^2), moran_test = unname(moran.test(v, lw4)$estimate[1])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` by_hand moran_test 0.5384615 0.5384615 ``` ::: ::: The two large values sit next to each other, so I is strongly positive. The function and the formula agree. ## On the district ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mi <- moran.test(blocks$dengue_per_100k, lw, zero.policy = TRUE) mi ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Moran I test under randomisation data: blocks$dengue_per_100k weights: lw Moran I statistic standard deviate = 7.4403, p-value = 5.025e-14 alternative hypothesis: greater sample estimates: Moran I statistic Expectation Variance 0.499247498 -0.012820513 0.004736744 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} Read it from the bottom: **observed I** (about 0.5), its **expectation** (about 0), and the **z-score and p-value**. Strong positive spatial autocorrelation. ::: ## The permutation (Monte Carlo) test Shuffle the values over the areas 999 times; how often does a shuffled map beat the real I? ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(1) mc <- moran.mc(blocks$dengue_per_100k, lw, nsim = 999, zero.policy = TRUE) ggplot(tibble(I = mc$res[-length(mc$res)]), aes(I)) + geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "grey75", colour = "white") + geom_vline(xintercept = mc$statistic, colour = col_red, linewidth = 1) + labs(x = "Moran's I of shuffled maps", title = paste0("Observed I (red) vs 999 shuffles: p = ", mc$p.value)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s3_global_autocorrelation_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - Assumption-light; usually the better p-value to report - With 999 shuffles the **smallest p is 0.001** ::: # Topic 2 — The Moran scatterplot {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Value against the average of its neighbours ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} blocks$z <- as.numeric(scale(blocks$dengue_per_100k)); blocks$lag_z <- lag.listw(lw, blocks$z, zero.policy = TRUE) ggplot(blocks, aes(z, lag_z)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") + geom_point(aes(colour = high_burden), size = 2.4) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "black") + annotate("text", x = c(2.2, -2.2, 2.2, -2.2), y = c(2.2, -2.2, -2.2, 2.2), label = c("High-High", "Low-Low", "High-Low", "Low-High"), colour = "grey40") + labs(x = "Rate (standardised)", y = "Neighbours' average (standardised)", colour = NULL) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s3_global_autocorrelation_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - The **slope of the line is Moran's I** (here 0.5) - **High-High / Low-Low** points make positive autocorrelation - **High-Low / Low-High** points are **spatial outliers**: LISA (Session 4) finds them ::: # Topic 3 — Other global tests {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Which global test? | Test | Question | Variable | Reading | |---|---|---|---| | **Moran's I** | Are similar values neighbours? | continuous | I > E[I]: clustering | | **Geary's C** | Are neighbours' *differences* small? | continuous | **C < 1** clustering (opposite of I) | | **General G** | Do **high** or **low** values cluster? | continuous, positive | G > E[G]: highs cluster | | **Join counts** | Do same-category areas touch? | binary / categorical | more same-category joins than expected | ## Geary's C, General G, join counts ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} geary.test(blocks$dengue_per_100k, lw, zero.policy = TRUE)$estimate ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Geary C statistic Expectation Variance 0.466797918 1.000000000 0.004855649 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} lw_b <- nb2listw(nb, style = "B", zero.policy = TRUE) globalG.test(blocks$dengue_per_100k, lw_b, zero.policy = TRUE)$estimate ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Global G statistic Expectation Variance 7.320125e-02 6.718598e-02 3.916081e-06 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} joincount.test(blocks$high_burden, lw_b, zero.policy = TRUE)[[2]]$estimate ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Same colour statistic Expectation Variance 39.00000 18.54333 10.97242 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} Moran's I is **positive for both hot-spot and cold-spot clustering**. Only **General G** says whether the **high** values are the ones that cluster. Join counts suit a **yes/no** variable. ::: ## Pitfalls ::: {.bad} - Not saying **which weights**; not saying **which variable** (counts and rates differ) - **Small areas** give noisy rates, which hides or mimics clustering (smooth with empirical Bayes) - **Edge effects** and the **modifiable areal unit problem**: a different grouping can change I - A **trend** (north-south gradient) also gives positive I - A global test **cannot say where**; a non-significant I can hide a local cluster ::: ## How to report ::: {.good} *Dengue incidence was strongly clustered across the 79 blocks (global Moran's I = 0.50, queen contiguity, row-standardised weights; permutation p = 0.001, 999 simulations).* ::: Give the statistic, the weights, the number of simulations and the p-value; then say where, with local methods. ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 3 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `gis-workshop/labs/lab3_global.R` - `moran.test()` · `moran.mc()` · the Moran scatterplot data - `geary.test()` · `globalG.test()` · `joincount.test()` - a variable with **no** spatial pattern for comparison ::: **Time:** 35 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s3q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="jtwbia.so757r" data-show="TmVpZ2hib3VyaW5nIGFyZWFzIGFyZSBtb3JlIGFsaWtlIHRoYW4gZXhwZWN0ZWQgYnkgY2hh bmNl" data-explain="QSBwb3NpdGl2ZSBJIHdpdGggYSBzbWFsbCBwLXZhbHVlIG1lYW5zIHNpbWlsYXIgdmFsdWVz IGFyZSBuZWlnaGJvdXJzIG1vcmUgb2Z0ZW4gdGhhbiByYW5kb20uIEl0IGlzIG5vdCBhIHBl cmNlbnRhZ2Ugb2YgdmFyaWFuY2UgZXhwbGFpbmVkIGFuZCBzYXlzIG5vdGhpbmcgYWJvdXQg d2hpY2ggYXJlYXMgZm9ybSBjbHVzdGVycy4="} Global Moran's I is 0.49 (permutation p = 0.001). What is the best interpretation? - 49% of the variation in the rate is explained by the location - Each area's rate is 0.49 higher than its neighbours' average rate - Neighbouring areas are more alike than expected by chance - About half of all the areas lie in a significant local cluster ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s3q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="jtwoqy.so7jp3" data-show="QWJvdXQgMCAoZXhhY3RseSDiiJIxLyhu4oiSMSkp" data-explain="VW5kZXIgcmFuZG9tbmVzcyBJIGhhcyBleHBlY3RhdGlvbiDiiJIxLyhu4oiSMSksIHdoaWNo IGlzIGNsb3NlIHRvIDAgZm9yIGFueSByZWFsaXN0aWMgbnVtYmVyIG9mIGFyZWFzLg=="} What is the expected value of Moran's I when there is no spatial pattern? - Exactly 1, because every area is its own neighbour - About 0 (exactly −1/(n−1)) - Exactly 0.5, halfway between the two extremes - It depends on the data, so there is no expected value ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s3q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="jtx1zo.so7y6h" data-show="MC4wMDEsIGFzIHRoZSBvYnNlcnZlZCB2YWx1ZSBpcyBvbmUgb2YgMTAwMCBhcnJhbmdlbWVu dHM=" data-explain="VGhlIG9ic2VydmVkIHN0YXRpc3RpYyBpcyByYW5rZWQgYW1vbmcgdGhlIDk5OSBzaHVmZmxl cyBwbHVzIGl0c2VsZiwgc28gdGhlIGJlc3QgcmFuayBnaXZlcyAoMCsxKS8oOTk5KzEpID0g MC4wMDEu"} With 999 permutations, what is the smallest possible p-value from moran.mc()? - 0, if the observed I is larger than every one of the shuffled values - 0.05, which is the usual cut-off used for a significant result - 0.001, as the observed value is one of 1000 arrangements - It varies from one data set to another and has no fixed minimum ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s3q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="jtxf8e.so8cnv" data-show="TmVpZ2hib3VycyBhcmUgc2ltaWxhciwgc28gcG9zaXRpdmUgc3BhdGlhbCBhdXRvY29ycmVs YXRpb24=" data-explain="QyBpcyBhYm91dCAxIHdpdGggbm8gcGF0dGVybiwgYmVsb3cgMSB3aXRoIHBvc2l0aXZlIGF1 dG9jb3JyZWxhdGlvbiBhbmQgYWJvdmUgMSB3aXRoIG5lZ2F0aXZlIGF1dG9jb3JyZWxhdGlv bi4gSXQgcnVucyBpbiB0aGUgb3Bwb3NpdGUgZGlyZWN0aW9uIHRvIE1vcmFuJ3MgSS4="} Geary's C is 0.47. How should this be read? - Neighbours differ strongly, so negative spatial autocorrelation - There is no spatial pattern, because C is not equal to zero - The result is invalid, because C must lie between 0 and 1 - Neighbours are similar, so positive spatial autocorrelation ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s3q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="jtxsh0.so8r55" data-show="V2hldGhlciBoaWdoIHZhbHVlcyAoaG90IHNwb3RzKSBvciBsb3cgdmFsdWVzIGNsdXN0ZXI=" data-explain="Qm90aCBob3Qtc3BvdCBhbmQgY29sZC1zcG90IGNsdXN0ZXJpbmcgZ2l2ZSBhIHBvc2l0aXZl IE1vcmFuJ3MgSS4gRyBpcyBhYm92ZSBpdHMgZXhwZWN0YXRpb24gd2hlbiBoaWdoIHZhbHVl cyBjbHVzdGVyIGFuZCBiZWxvdyB3aGVuIGxvdyB2YWx1ZXMgZG8u"} Moran's I is positive and significant. What does the General G test add? - Whether high values (hot spots) or low values cluster - The exact location of each separate cluster on the map - A correction of the p-value for the multiple testing - Nothing, because it always gives the same answer as Moran's I ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **Moran's I**: are similar values neighbours? Compare with about 0 - Prefer the **permutation p-value**; always give the **weights** - The **Moran scatterplot** shows slope = I and the four quadrants - **Geary's C** (1 = none), **General G** (hot vs cold), **join counts** (binary) ::: **Next:** Session 4: local clusters and hot spots

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
